L299: ### `GET` /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns
L300: 
L301: List outreach campaigns
L302: List the outreach campaigns owned by your organization. Authenticated by the same `X-API-Key` as the rest of this API — the key resolves to your organization, and campaigns are returned across all of its projects. Pass `project_id` (see `GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/projects`) to get one project's campaigns only. **Response:** - `campaigns` — non-archived campaigns with `id`, `project_id`, `name`, `target_url`, `daily_limit_usd`, and lifecycle `status`. - `total` — number of campaigns returned.
L303: Use a campaign `id` to scope follow-up management calls (inbox replies, budget, start/stop, analytics).
L304: #### Parameters
L305: 
L306:   * `project_id` (query, optional): Return only this project's campaigns (see `GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/projects`).
L307: #### Responses
L308:   * `200`: Successful Response
L309:   * `401`: Invalid or missing API key. Include `X-API-Key` header.
L310:   * `402`: Insufficient credit balance. Every request needs a positive balance, including requests that fall entirely inside the free results zone. Top up your account.
L311:   * `422`: Validation error. Check request body and parameters.
L312:   * `429`: Rate limit exceeded (10000/hour), concurrent limit reached (150 per organization), or free preview quota exceeded (search requests entirely within the free results zone; the quota depends on your plan).

L316: ### `POST` /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns
L317: 
L318: Create campaign
L319: Create a campaign that Explee finds the leads for — the app's **New campaign** button. Only `project_id` and `name` are required. Explee drafts every targeting field you leave out (offer, customer problem, criteria, example clients) from the name and your project; a field you send replaces the draft (`[]` means "none"). Search `keywords` are always drafted from the name. Geography and company size default to the project's. Not idempotent: each call creates a new campaign.
L320: If a call times out, list the project's campaigns before retrying. **Lifecycle after this call** (`status` in `GET /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns`): 1. `discovery` — created, nothing runs yet. Review or edit it with `GET` / `PATCH /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}`. 2. `POST …/campaigns/{campaign_id}/start` — Explee searches for leads. Works with Auto-manage campaigns on or off. 3. `review` — the lead list is ready. Approve it with `POST …/campaigns/{campaign_id}/approve`.
L321: With Auto-manage campaigns ON it is also approved automatically at the end of the project's review window (12 hours by default); with it OFF only `approve` sends it. 4. `outreach` — sending, within the campaign and project budgets. `POST …/stop` at any point parks the campaign (`listening`); a later `start` resumes it — from a stopped review that means sending without a further approve. Creation is free. Returns the campaign's full definition.

L324: Request body required

L326:   * `201`: Successful Response
L327:   * `401`: Invalid or missing API key. Include `X-API-Key` header.
L328:   * `402`: Insufficient credit balance. Every request needs a positive balance, including requests that fall entirely inside the free results zone. Top up your account.
L329:   * `422`: Validation error. Check request body and parameters.
L330:   * `429`: Rate limit exceeded (10000/hour), concurrent limit reached (150 per organization), or free preview quota exceeded (search requests entirely within the free results zone; the quota depends on your plan).
L331:   * `500`: Internal server error. Contact support if persists.
L332:   * `504`: Request timeout. Please try again later.
L333:   * `404`: Unknown `project_id` (or not your project).
L334:   * `409`: The project is paused for review by Explee.
L335:   * `503`: Drafting the campaign failed — retry.
L336: ### `GET` /public/api/v1/autogtm/campaigns/{campaign_id}
L337: 
L338: Get campaign definition
L339: Read everything that decides who a campaign contacts and what it says — the app's **Campaign** tab in one call. **Who it targets:** `offer`, `customer_problem`, `target_role`, `target_geography`, `target_company_size`, `positive_criteria`, `negative_criteria`, `example_clients`, and the derived `keywords`. **What it says:** `instructions` (first email), `followup_instructions` (shared by every follow-up), `language`, and the project-level `reply_instructions`.
L340: **When it says it:** `schedule` (the send days) and `followups` (how many emails the sequence has and how far apart — a project-level setting, the same for every campaign of the project). `targeting_editable` is `false` for a campaign built from your own imported lead list — its audience is that list, so the targeting fields are locked. Free, and the natural first call when auditing an account: one request per campaign tells you whether it is aimed at the right people, before a single email goes out.

L641: 
L642: Set campaign daily budget
L643: Set one campaign's daily budget. L749: ### `POST` /public/api/v1/autogtm/suppress-list/people
L750: 
L751: Suppress people
L752: Store a list of people to suppress — the same lists the **Suppress list** page in the app shows, so a list pushed from your CRM sits next to the CSVs your team uploaded and behaves identically. The suppress list is organization-wide: it applies to **every** outreach campaign, running or not. Every email is checked against it right before it goes out, so an address added here stops a sequence that is already mid-flight, not just future ones.
L753: Matching is exact: a person by their email address (case-insensitive, but `【0†[email protected]】` and `【0†[email protected]】` are two different entries), a company by its domain (the lead's company domain or the domain of its email address — `acme.com` does not cover `eu.acme.com`, list each domain you use).
L754: One call = one list, exactly like uploading one CSV: a `list` name that is already taken gets a `(2)` suffix rather than merging, and lists are independent — the same person on two lists is suppressed until both are gone. Delete a list you no longer want. Each person needs at least one identifier: an email, a LinkedIn URL, or a full name; a row left without a usable one (including a malformed address) comes back in `skipped` instead of failing the whole batch.
L755: **Outreach stops on the email** — the name and LinkedIn fields are stored but not actively used today; they are kept because a suppressed person is more than their email address, and the day outreach runs somewhere other than email (LinkedIn and the like) those are the fields that will match. To suppress everyone at a company use the companies endpoint.
